Anna (Platform): Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a small 'translation playbook' to normalize config/ops between hosted / dedicated / private. Aim: fewer bespoke shims, clearer responsibilities for control plane vs runtime, and predictable fallbacks.
Mike (Runtime): Can you sketch the main surface? my worry: we can't hide hardware-dependent knobs completely (quant, kernels, batching) — those affect latency/cost SLOs.
Priya (Eng-Infra): +1 to a playbook. We need explicit KMS/audit/auth boundaries. Private installs will always require different key exchange flows. That should be a named capability, not ad-hoc.
Dan (Product): Customers expect the same API surface. If we require feature flags or different routes, we need to make that invisible to app devs. So the playbook must include stable API compatibility rules.
Sasha (SRE): Also: telemetry shapes differ. Hosted -> our tracing headers, private -> customer-side tracing. Playbook should define telemetry translation points and what we can sample/retain.
Anna (Platform): Proposed minimal spec: 1) capability negotiation at attach time (list of opt-in capabilities). 2) a short 'translation table' for config keys (what maps to what). 3) fallback policies with priority ordering.
Mike (Runtime): Capability negotiation sounds good. Example: runtime reports "supports-prefetch-kv", "quant-8". Router picks best compatible variant. But we need deterministic selection rules.
Priya (Eng-Infra): For key mapping I suggest a canonical key namespace in the control plane, then short mapping files per deployment type. Example mapping snippet: ```json
{
  "cache.prefix_ttl": "kv_cache.ttl",
  "batch.max_tokens": "runtime.batch_cap"
}
```
Dan (Product): That mapping approach is fine as long as it never changes behavior for hosted customers unexpectedly. Version the mapping files and include a migration policy.
Sasha (SRE): On fallbacks: propose ordering: same-model-variant -> cheaper-variant (quantized) -> regional-fallback -> capacity-throttle with queued response. Each step should have observable metric labels.
Anna (Platform): Good point on observability. Add to playbook: a standard set of labels for fallbacks: `redwood.fallback.reason`, `redwood.fallback.step`, `redwood.fallback.duration`.
Mike (Runtime): One operational tradeoff: exposing fine-grained capability flags increases surface area for compatibility testing. We should group them into stable capability tiers (CORE, PERF, EXPERIMENTAL).
Priya (Eng-Infra): Agreed — CORE must be available in all deployment modes. PERF can be negotiated. EXPERIMENTAL requires opt-in and will be disabled by default in Private.
Dan (Product): How will rollouts work? If we change mapping or capability tiering, we need a canary that simulates private installs without touching customer infra.
Anna (Platform): Idea: a 'sandbox private' mode in hosted where control-plane uses the private mapping rules but still runs on hosted infra. Good for smoke testing mappings and rollouts.
Sasha (SRE): Please ensure the playbook mandates a failure-mode that preserves correctness over perf. For example, if a perf capability is missing, we must never silently degrade to a model with different outputs — only degrade perf (latency/cost), not quality.
Mike (Runtime): Practical note: some models behave differently when quantized. The playbook must include a quality regression checkset per model that runs on every candidate mapping change.
Priya (Eng-Infra): Security: mapping files and capability vectors must be signed and audited. Private installs should fetch mapping files via configured endpoints only. Put that in the control-plane responsibilities section.
Dan (Product): Also include a short UX blurb: admin-facing docs describing what 'missing capability' means and what remediation steps are. Keep it concise.
Anna (Platform): I'll draft a lightweight playbook doc with sections: goals, capability tiers, canonical keys, mapping format, fallback order, observability labels, rollout/testing checklist, security signing. I'll post a PR.
Mike (Runtime): +1 — please include an example of the negotiation handshake (proto) and deterministic selection algo.
Priya (Eng-Infra): I'll add the KMS/audit flow examples and a signed-mapping format.
Sasha (SRE): I'll add the SLO safeguard rules and required metrics.
Dan (Product): I'll review for product impact and customer-facing wording.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: infra/routing-service v1.14.3 -> staging :rocket:
Anna (Platform): Thanks all. We'll keep the playbook intentionally small to avoid scope creep. I'll tag owners in the PR. :thumbsup:
